gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Creality's $1,606 'Otter Lite + 3D Printer (All-In-One Combo)' page never names the printer it includes, or that buying the parts separately from the makers today costs $594–$664: a 3DMakerpro Seal Lite (rated 0.02 mm, $215) plus a QIDI Q2 ($449) or Flashforge AD5M Pro ($379). That is about what ChatGPT's own budget pair cost ($658.99), but its Creality Ferret SE scanner is rated only 0.1 mm.
standout_why: I compared against these pages. Creality's scanner-combo collection and its K2 Plus and Otter Lite combo pages (cited) show prices, but their 'Combo Details' sections are empty: they name no printer and give no build volume or scanner accuracy. The K2 Plus page also shows $1,799, while the collection lists it at $2,699. 3dprintmates lists only scanners, with no printers and no combined price. rottenwifi says integrated machines are 'uncommon' and gives only $1,500–$2,500 planning bands. It names no pairing under $700, and Seal Lite, Flashforge and the Otter Lite combo are absent. No rival puts the makers' accuracy ratings next to the total price of a scan-and-print setup.
decides: It moves the budget pick away from a Creality bundle and toward two separate devices. Seal Lite + QIDI Q2 ($664) or Seal Lite + AD5M Pro ($594) cost about the same as ChatGPT's A1 Combo + Ferret SE ($658.99). The makers rate the Seal Lite scanner 5× tighter (0.02 mm vs 0.1 mm). It also costs $942–$1,012 less than the $1,606 Otter Lite combo, whose printer the page doesn't name. That combo loses because you can't tell what printer you get. Pay K2 Plus or Raptor-combo prices only if you need to scan large objects.
